title: MLB calibration is improving month over month -- but still trails the market
headline_insight: The MLB model's calibration error fell from 0.1165 in June to 0.0834 in July, yet the market stayed sharper in both months (0.0944, then 0.0635).
what_it_means: Splitting the record by calendar month checks whether the model is stable or drifting. MLB is encouraging -- the model got better-calibrated as July games came in (ECE 0.1165 to 0.0834) -- but the market improved in lockstep and kept its lead. Soccer went the other way: the model's monthly Brier climbed from 0.1729 to 0.331.
how_to_read: Each cell is one sport-month; lower Brier and ECE are better, and the honest comparison is the model row against the market row within the same month.
why_it_matters: A model whose numbers hold steady across months is trustworthy; one whose numbers swing (soccer) needs more data before any monthly split can be believed.
caveat: July soccer rests on only n=3129 rows, so its worse numbers may reflect a small, harder sample rather than genuine month-over-month degradation.
